questions.question_text: Statement I: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than the eclipsed conformation. Statement II: The torsional strain in staggered conformation is more. Read the above statements and choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.question_html:
Statement I: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than the eclipsed conformation.
Statement II: The torsional strain in staggered conformation is more.
Read the above statements and choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.html: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.html: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.html: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: D
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.html: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.explanation_text: Statement I is true. In ethane, the staggered conformation is more stable because the hydrogen atoms on the two carbon atoms are as far apart as possible. The dihedral angle between C-H bonds is $60^{\circ}$ , so the repulsion between bonding electron pairs is minimum. Statement II is false. Torsional strain is not more in the staggered conformation. It is maximum in the eclipsed conformation because the C-H bonds of the two carbon atoms are directly aligned with each other. This causes greater repulsion between bonding electron pairs. So, $\text{Statement I is true but Statement II is false.}$ Correct answer: Option C.
questions.explanation_html:
Statement I is true.

In ethane, the staggered conformation is more stable because the hydrogen atoms on the two carbon atoms are as far apart as possible. The dihedral angle between C-H bonds is $60^{\circ}$ , so the repulsion between bonding electron pairs is minimum.

Statement II is false.

Torsional strain is not more in the staggered conformation. It is maximum in the eclipsed conformation because the C-H bonds of the two carbon atoms are directly aligned with each other. This causes greater repulsion between bonding electron pairs.

So,

$\text{Statement I is true but Statement II is false.}$

Correct answer: Option C.

questions.question_text: For the preparation of alkanes, aqueous solution of sodium of potassium salt of carboxylic acid is subjected to
questions.question_html: For the preparation of alkanes, aqueous solution of sodium of potassium salt of carboxylic acid is subjected to

options.label: A
options.html: hydrolysis

options.label: B
options.html: electrolysis

options.label: C
options.html: hydrogenation

options.label: D
options.html: oxidation

questions.explanation_text: The correct answer is Option B: electrolysis . This process is known as Kolbe electrolysis. Here's why: Kolbe Electrolysis: When an aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of a carboxylic acid is electrolyzed, it results in the formation of an alkane. $2RCOO^{-}Na^{+}+2H_{2}O\overset{Electrolysis}{\rightarrow \le ftarrow}R-R+2CO_{2}+H_{2}+2NaOH$ In this reaction: The $RCOO^{-}$ part comes from the sodium or potassium salt of the carboxylic acid. Electrolysis involves passing an electric current through the solution. $R-R$ represents the alkane formed.
questions.explanation_html:
The correct answer is Option B: electrolysis. This process is known as Kolbe electrolysis.

Here's why:

Kolbe Electrolysis: When an aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of a carboxylic acid is electrolyzed, it results in the formation of an alkane.

$2RCOO^{-}Na^{+}+2H_{2}O\overset{Electrolysis}{\rightarrow \le ftarrow}R-R+2CO_{2}+H_{2}+2NaOH$

In this reaction:

The $RCOO^{-}$ part comes from the sodium or potassium salt of the carboxylic acid.

Electrolysis involves passing an electric current through the solution.

$R-R$ represents the alkane formed.
